column5: Gap real (only expository-writing at higher stage; opinion/narrative/descriptive early exist). Structure matches CCSS W.K-3.2 (name topic, facts, definitions, group related info, linking words also/another, concluding statement; headings at grade 4). Facts: tadpole stage, shark tooth rows, owl silent flight all standard. Prereqs exist; hard prereq writing-complete-sentences concrete-operations = stage. Style clean.

Gap real (no early-grade affix/root topic; only linguistics prefix-suffix-affixation, derivational-morphology). Wrong: misconception said removing "re" from "read" leaves no real word, but "ad" is a word; changed to "no base word with a related meaning". Verified: graph < Greek graphein write/draw (autograph, paragraph < paragraphos, biography); port carry, dict say, rupt break, tele far, phon sound, bio life; indestructible < Latin in- + destruere (de- + struere, build); un- 'not' vs un- 'reverse' (Etymonline). Prereqs exist; stage ok.

Gap real (no homophone/usage topic; apostrophe and possessive-pronoun topics touch its/it's only). Wrong: (1) "possessive pronouns take/never use an apostrophe" is false for one's, someone's etc.; narrowed to personal possessive pronouns (misconception and Explainer). (2) "Spell-checkers rarely help" overstated (contextual checkers catch many); changed to "often miss these errors". Verified: CCSS L.4.1g frequently confused words (to/too/two, there/their); it's = it is/it has; affect noun (psychology) and effect verb (bring about) per Merriam-Webster; than/then, accept/except, lose/loose, principal/principle. Questions correct. Hard prereq stage concrete-operations = stage.

Gap real (subjunctive-mood only covers "if I were"; no conditional topic). Wrong: "Both [if it will rain / if I would have known] occur often in speech" overstated for the first, which is mainly a learner error; split into learner error vs casual-speech error. Verified: zero/first/second/third + mixed conditional patterns (Cambridge, British Council grammar); CGEL "modal remoteness" past tense; irrealis/subjunctive were; inversion with had/were/should; CCSS L.8.1c. Questions correct. Hard prereqs exist, highest abstract-reasoning = stage.

Gap real (vocabulary-context-clues mentions synonyms only as a clue type; semantic-relations is formal-systems). Matches CCSS L.K-5.5 (K.5b verbs/adjectives with opposites; 1.5d/2.5b shades of meaning e.g. toss/throw/hurl, thin/slender/skinny; 4.5c synonyms/antonyms). All question keys and word senses (light, bat, ring, nibble/devour) correct. Prereqs exist; stage ok. Style clean.

Gap real (spoken-language-basics covers pre-formal turn-taking only; panel-discussion-skills is public-speaking). Verified: CCSS SL.1 "participate in collaborative conversations" in every grade K-12; come prepared (SL.3.1a), agreed-upon rules (SL.1.1a/SL.2.1a), build on others' talk (SL.1.1b), explain ideas in light of the discussion (SL.3.1d), review key ideas (SL.5.1d). Questions correct. Style only: rewrote misconception 1 correction that used the "is not X; the skill is Y" frame. Prereqs exist; stage ok.

Gap real (no quotation-punctuation topic covers ellipsis/brackets/[sic]; quotation-integration-writing does not mention them). Wrong: [sic] example was not a quotation and put [sic] at sentence end instead of right after the error; replaced with a quoted misspelling followed by [sic]. Verified: CCSS L.8.2b ellipsis for omission; MLA/APA/Chicago spaced ellipsis, four dots at sentence end, no ellipsis needed at start/end of fragment quotations; sic = Latin "thus/so"; brackets for insertions, [T] capitalization change (Purdue OWL, Chicago). Questions correct. Hard prereq abstract-reasoning = stage.

Gap real (countability only mentioned in passing in articles-a-an-the-usage and irregular-plural-nouns-common). Wrong: "Formal style still prefers 'fewer' there" (in "10 items or less") overstates; Merriam-Webster and most usage guides accept "or less" after numbers; reworded to accept the fixed phrase while recommending fewer before plural count nouns. Verified: count/noncount tests, unit words, many/much, few/little, number/amount; French "informations" countable; dual-class nouns (paper, glass, chicken, time, light). Questions correct. Style: softened "is not about the real world". Prereqs exist; stage ok.

Gap real: expository-writing covers process analysis in one paragraph as a mode, while sibling modes (compare-and-contrast-writing) have their own topics; this file adds directive vs informative types, materials, staging, warnings, reader testing. Verified: directive/informative process distinction (standard in patterns-of-development readers, e.g. Kirszner and Mandell "instructions" vs "process explanation"); resting dough relaxes gluten; root loosening advice. Questions correct. Hard prereq expository-writing abstract-reasoning = stage. Style clean.

Gap real (no classification topic; expository-writing mentions "definition/classification" in one clause). Verified: division (one whole into parts) vs classification (many items into groups), single principle, mutually exclusive and sufficiently complete categories, thesis with a point (standard in Kirszner and Mandell, Purdue OWL). Questions correct (only option 3 uses one principle). Style only: cut "not just that they exist" from Core Idea. Hard prereqs abstract-reasoning = stage.

Gap real (rhetorical-purpose-and-intention is writing-focused; speech-structure-and-organization only mentions central idea). Verified against Lucas ch. "Selecting a Topic and a Purpose" summaries (McGraw-Hill chapter summary, LibreTexts Barton and Tucker 4.04): general purpose inform/persuade, special-occasion entertain/commemorate; specific purpose as infinitive phrase, statement not question, one distinct idea, not vague, achievable in time; central idea as one-sentence message often previewing main points. Questions correct. No hard prereqs; formal-systems matches soft prereq audience-analysis-for-speaking and college course level. Style clean.

Gap real (Hockett appears nowhere else in the language domain). Verified: Hockett 1960 "The Origin of Speech" (Sci. Am. 203(3)), 13 features later expanded to 16 (Hockett and Altmann 1968); arbitrariness, displacement, productivity, duality of patterning, traditional/cultural transmission, vocal-auditory channel, interchangeability, rapid fading, discreteness (Wikipedia, U. Oregon handout); Stokoe 1960 ASL; von Frisch waggle dance direction and distance; vervet leopard/eagle/snake calls (Seyfarth, Cheney, Marler 1980); Washoe, Kanzi. Questions correct. All ids exist; stage formal-systems fits intro college linguistics. Style clean.

Gap real (no acoustic phonetics topic; formants appear only in psychology coarticulation and signal-processing topics). Verified: source-filter model (Fant 1960, Acoustic Theory of Speech Production); F0 = pitch, harmonics at multiples; F1 inverse to height, F2 to backness, rounding lowers formants; adult male /i/ ~270/2290 Hz, /u/ ~300/870 Hz (Peterson and Barney 1952 as tabulated at CCRMA; Hillenbrand 1995 /u/ F2 ~1000); hVd words; VOT definition and English aspirated /p/ vs short-lag /b/; spectrogram conventions; Praat free. Questions correct. Hard prereq articulatory-phonetics formal-systems = stage; sound-waves-intro exists (physics).

Gap real (history/historical-semantics-and-terminology-change is conceptual history; lexical-semantics mentions change once). Wrong/unsupported: "most familiar English words have shifted meaning at least once" (no source for "most"); changed to "many familiar English words, such as nice, meat, silly". Verified (Etymonline, OED summaries): deor 'animal', mete 'food', girl ME either sex, holiday < holy day, docga/dogge used for a powerful breed (Etymonline), cniht 'boy, servant', nice < OFr < Lat nescius, gesaelig 'happy, blessed', villain 'farm laborer', hussy < housewife, decimate Roman one-in-ten; etymological fallacy; metonymy crown/press; going to > future. Questions correct. Hard prereq historical-linguistics formal-systems = stage.

Gap real (literature/old-english-literature-and-beowulf is literary; historical-linguistics has one passing mention). Verified: West Germanic, Angles/Saxons/Jutes 5th c.; OE/ME/EModE period boundaries (c.1100, c.1500, c.1700); Augustine's mission 597; Viking raids from late 8th c., Danelaw; Norse sky, egg, skin, they/them/their; Norman Conquest 1066, French law/government/food words (beef, pork); Chaucer late 14th c.; Caxton press at Westminster 1476 (Westminster Abbey, Wikipedia); KJV 1611; Johnson 1755; GVS /i:/,/u:/ > diphthongs, others raise (ME /e:/ in meet > /i:/); kingly/royal/regal and ask/question/interrogate (Baugh and Cable). Questions correct. Hard prereq formal-systems = stage.

Gap real (creoles only mentioned in passing in language-universals, universal-grammar-hypothesis; anthropology creolization is cultural). Wrong (imprecise): "algebra" taken "through Arabic" - it is from Arabic al-jabr by way of Medieval Latin; reworded. Verified: Wolkenkratzer calque of skyscraper; flea market / marche aux puces; ketchup probably from Hokkien; Haitian Creole co-official with French (1987 constitution); Hawai'i Creole English called Pidgin; Tok Pisin official in PNG, -pela < fellow; Bickerton bioprogram (1981); substrate, lexifier, creole continuum; preverbal TMA markers. Questions correct. Style: removed banned "Crucially". Hard prereq sociolinguistics-intro formal-systems = stage.

Gap real (politeness only in passing in linguistic-pragmatics, conversation-analysis, philosophy indirect-speech-acts). Verified: Goffman face (1955 "On Face-Work"); Brown and Levinson 1978 (in Goody, Questions and Politeness) reissued 1987 as Politeness: Some Universals in Language Usage; positive/negative face; FTAs incl. apology threatening speaker's positive face; five superstrategies (bald on record, positive, negative, off record, don't do FTA); weight = D + P + R; bald on record under urgency; Matsumoto 1988 / Ide 1989 Japanese discernment critique. Questions correct. Hard prereq speech-act-theory formal-systems = stage. Style clean.

Gap real (Lakoff/Tannen appear only here; other Lakoff hits are George Lakoff metaphor). Verified: Lakoff, Language and Woman's Place 1975 (hedges, tags, empty adjectives, intensifiers, hypercorrect grammar); deficit/dominance/difference framings; Zimmerman and West 1975 interruptions; Tannen 1990 You Just Don't Understand; Eckert and McConnell-Ginet communities of practice (1992); Labov gender paradox (Principles of Linguistic Change vol. 2); Mehl et al. 2007 Science, 396 students, EAR over several days, ~16,215 vs 15,669 words/day, n.s. (UT news, Wilson Quarterly); Maedchen neuter. Questions correct. Hard prereqs formal-systems = stage.

Gap real (no Construction Grammar topic; Goldberg/let alone appear nowhere else). Verified: Fillmore, Kay and O'Connor 1988 "let alone" (Language 64(3), cited p.504); Kay and Fillmore 1999 What's X doing Y; comparative correlative; Goldberg 1995 Constructions (U Chicago Press), sneezed the napkin off the table / foam off the cappuccino, caused-motion and ditransitive constructions, coercion; constructicon; Berkeley CxG and SBCG (feature structures), Croft Radical CxG 2001; Tomasello item-based/usage-based acquisition (course notes, Steels 2011). Questions correct. stage expert matches sibling advanced-linguistics topics; hard prereqs formal-systems.
